HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Romance still, medium-close two-shot, low angle against the morning sky, beside a stone village well with a timber well-beam and hanging rope bucket. Young Jumong (rugged archer, bare-headed, red robe with the sleeves pushed up over strong forearms, broad back) has Sosuno backed against the well-beam and kisses her, one big hand at her jaw, the other at her waist. Sosuno (dusty-rose jeogori and skirt, the cloth soaked dark from the rope at her waist and clinging tight to her waist and hips) has rope still wound in one fist and the other hand fisted in his collar, kissing him back hard, ears pink. Water slops over the bucket lip and splashes the stones. ONE device: the over-full bucket spilling beside them. Red #e8563f on him, dusty-rose #e8a04a on her, cool morning light. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = jumong, SECOND face = sosuno. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board sosuno (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). JUMONG — Look: Lean archer; black hair half-bound under a knotted red headband with long tails; dark warm eyes, easy grin. CLEAN-SHAVEN before he is king — ignore the moustache and chin hair on his portrait. Dress: Red silk jeogori and po over a charcoal underlayer, rope-tied sash, wrapped forearms; bow across his back. Crown: Goguryeo gold crown: a gold band crowded with upright flame and branch sprays hung with small round gold spangles; at court the king may instead wear the tall silk cap of the king on the costume chart. Colour #e8563f. SOSUNO — Look: Long straight black hair with a high topknot pinned by her gold binyeo, a thin red headband with a center jewel; sharp brows, cool appraising eyes. Dress: Dusty-rose hanbok over white sleeves, black wrap sash with red cords, red-wrapped wrists; bow and quiver on her back. Her hex is lamplight or a ground stamp — never gold robes. Colour #e8a04a. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
